PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: ward-jesus-belt
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Wardrobe guard: transfer only textile rendering, light response, practical aging, and filmic material quality. Do not introduce white burial linen, blood, sandals, or a body identity unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
JESUS CHRIST — LEATHER CORD BELT — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: COSTUME CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, FIT, DAMAGE, AND CONTINUITY.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Four-view cinematic wardrobe ingredients sheet isolating the leather cord belt of Jesus the Harrower for the biblical epic JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL. This is a production construction reference for a simple, humble first-century Judean waist cord—not a modern fashion belt, not a plated buckle, not ornate metalwork—cinching the white linen ankle-length robe at the natural waist of a Mediterranean man approximately five feet ten inches tall with an athletic, unexaggerated build.

Subject of the sheet: the belt itself as the primary hero object, shown worn on a neutral headless or soft-focus matching torso silhouette of Jesus (olive Mediterranean skin, clean male torso proportions consistent with the character canon) so scale and drape against white linen read correctly. In every panel the belt is the locked continuity piece: same length, same thickness, same knot style, same leather color and wear map. One face only exists on the front of any head if a head is partially visible; prefer framing that keeps attention on the midsection and belt construction. No second face on the rear of the head.

Material identity: hand-twisted natural leather cord, roughly 8–12 millimeters in diameter when twisted, formed from tanned animal hide of a warm dark brown to deep umber tone with cooler ash-brown undertones in the shadows. Surface shows honest organic irregularity—fine hair follicle texture in the leather grain, slight variation in twist tightness along its length, microscopic cracks at stress points, and a matte-to-satin waxed sheen only where hands have repeatedly gripped and adjusted the knot. Not polished designer leather; not black patent; not dyed synthetic. Edges of the cord show soft, slightly frayed fiber where hide was cut and worked by hand. Occasional pale salt-like mineral flecks and a faint dust of desert grit cling in the twists, continuity with the journey from Golgotha through the desert night into hell’s fortress.

Construction and knot: the belt is a single long cord wrapped once around the waist over the gathered linen, finished with a practical functional knot at the front-center or slightly off-center toward the wearer’s right—a simple overhand or figure knot with two short free ends hanging downward along the robe, each end roughly the length of a man’s hand from palm to fingertips. Ends are cut clean then naturally softened by wear, not metal-capped, not fringed with decorative tassels, not braided into ornate macramé. Optional subtle secondary wrap tuck if the cord is long enough, but the silhouette remains humble and uncluttered. The cord compresses the white linen into soft vertical folds above and below the waistline; fabric gathers in natural pleats without theatrical bulk.

Wear and continuity with blood/robe map: the belt itself may carry faint contact stains—minute dark reddish-brown blood transfer near the left side of the waist where the side wound on Jesus’s torso can wick into linen and lightly touch the cord when the robe shifts; a faint darker grime band on the inner face of the cord where sweat and body oils have darkened the leather against skin and undergarment. Outer face of the cord remains largely clean, earthy brown, so it does not read as a bloody prop. These marks are subtle and photoreal, never gore-heavy. The belt must read identically across all Jesus shots: same knot orientation, same hanging end lengths, same leather color, same compression of the white robe.

Panel layout for the four-view ingredients sheet:
1) Frontal three-quarter midsection and belt close construction view—hero detail of knot, twist grain, hanging ends, linen gather, olive skin at the waist edge if visible under the robe opening, clean hands if a hand rests near the knot for scale only.
2) Full-body or three-quarter figure scale view—belt worn correctly on the white ankle-length linen robe with rough leather sandals visible at the feet for period continuity; athletic male silhouette; deliberate upright posture of absolute certainty; midsection is the focus of sharpness with natural falloff.
3) Side profile of the waist—shows how the cord sits on the natural waist curve, thickness of the twisted leather in profile, how hanging ends fall against the robe, and how linen folds stack above and below the cinch.
4) Rear / costume-back view—rear of the white robe at the waist with the cord continuous across the back, no decorative buckle plate, no modern logo hardware, single continuous leather twist; complete rear costume construction without inventing a second face.

Lighting for production reference: soft physically coherent key from slightly above and front-left, warm-neutral key around 4500–5000K to read true leather brown and white linen weave without crushing shadow detail; gentle fill from camera-right; subtle cool rim if needed to separate cord from robe. Prefer clean studio-neutral or soft stone-wall period-atelier background with shallow depth of field so the belt remains the sharp subject. Avoid pure hell-red underglow or pure divine gold god-rays as the sole lighting unless used as a faint secondary rim that still preserves material readability. No harsh modern beauty-ring glare. Volumetric haze kept minimal so leather microtexture and linen fiber remain sharp.

Camera and presentation: photoreal live-action cinematic production still language, equivalent to a 50–85mm portrait/macro hybrid for detail panels and roughly 35–50mm for the full-body scale panel; shallow to moderate depth of field with the leather twist and knot in critical focus; consistent scale across panels; 2.39:1 cinematic sensibility within the sheet composition where natural. Physically accurate materials, clean anatomy if hands or torso appear, no plastic CGI sheen, no illustration, no anime, no cartoon.

Color grade: restrained biblical-epic neutrals—warm brown leather, ivory-white linen with slight age cream, olive Mediterranean skin, soft grey-stone or parchment-neutral negative space. No neon, no modern fashion palette, no high-chroma fantasy saturation.

Texture and atmosphere: resolve leather grain, fiber twist, faint desert grit in the cord, linen weave translucency at the robe’s thinner areas, soft shadow in deep folds, realistic contact shadows under the hanging cord ends. Atmosphere is quiet and reverent—a wardrobe vault reference for a sacred epic, not a product catalog with price tags.

Hard constraints locked for continuity: leather cord belt only—no metal buckle, no modern webbing, no logos, no brand stamps, no readable text, no captions, no watermarks, no borders, no UI, no labels on the image. Same belt construction must match Jesus’s white linen robe and rough leather sandals canon. Humble first-century construction. Photoreal live-action only. One face only on the front of any head. No modern objects.
